newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed,as crosses dominate trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed,as crosses dominate trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed, as cash cross activity continued to dominate trade in the pits, traders and analysts said.
They said December yen's weak tone was directly attributed to the heavy buying of cash marks and Swiss francs against the yen.

One analyst said the 12.9-percent decline in Japan's October trade surplus led dealers and funds to buy back the cash marks they sold last week against the yen. Cash mark/yen rebounded back towards 74.30 after falling to 73.50 last week, and helped generate buying interest in mark futures.

Several traders also said the public offering of Deutsche Telecom shares this week continued to lift mark futures. One analyst speculated, however, that 60 percent of the marks needed to buy shares of the German phone company last week were bought last week.
Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke's comments late in the day that the German central bank would welcome a more stable and stronger dollar did little to pressure December marks.
The contract still closed above last Friday's high of $0.6659.

Traders are still smarting from comments made by Eisuke Sakakibara, key Japanese finance minister, a day after the U.S. Presidential election that suggested the dollar/yen's corrective rally may be over.
Traders remain confused about the G3's forex policy, despite reiterations from G3 officials, including Sakakibara, in the last week that their forex policy has not changed.
On Sunday night, Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan reaffirmed their countries' basic stance on forex policy, but declined to elaborate.
Greenspan will hold a news conference at 1830 CST/0030 GMT on Tuesday.
One bank trader said speculative accounts were still long yen, and would remain long as long as the dollar/yen holds above 110.00, or $0.009126 in December marks.
In fact, one floor trader believes dollar/yen will edge higher, possibly testing 111.75 spot, or $0.008984.
He is looking for dollar/yen to rise to 111.90 to 112.00 spot or $0.008971 to $0.008964 in December yen ahead of U.S. September trade data on Wednesday.
One U.S. firm sold 2,000 December Canadian dollars and sold about 1,600 June Canadian dollars after buying more than 6,500 June contracts last month.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000038 at $0.009000, marks were up $0.0031 at $0.6670, Swiss francs were up $0.0069 at $0.7909, sterling was $0.0066 higher at $1.6700, Canadian dollars were off $0.0019 at $0.7465, Aussie dollars rose $0.0031 at $0.7926 and pesos rose $0.000250 at $0.124150.
